jena: Quick flag — reranker-int8 shows inconsistent behavior across holdouts. On en-smoke it's +0.002 NDCG@10 vs fp16 but on multilingual-smoke it's -0.045. Same quant pipeline.

omar: That's weird. Are we using the same tokenizer model across languages? Any normalization changes (punctuation, unicode NFC/NFD)?

jena: We switched to the new shared tokenizer config `rerank-unified-v2` during onboarding. It normalizes punctuation for Latin scripts but left CJK unchanged. Eval commands: `./eval/run.py --model reranker-1b-int8 --holdout en-smoke --k 10` and `./eval/run.py --model reranker-1b-int8 --holdout multilingual-smoke --k 10`. Artifacts: https://console.redwood/jobs/55001 (both runs).

luke: Two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer config mismatch between fp16 and int8 containers (maybe fp16 uses legacy tokenizer), 2) punctuation normalization changed candidate text length distribution for non-Latin queries causing quantized attention scale mismatch.

omar: Can you run a tiny probe: feed multilingual-smoke through fp16 with the new tokenizer and compare NDCG to the old fp16 baseline? Command: `python tools/reencode.py --tokenizer rerank-unified-v2 --input multilingual-smoke.jsonl --out reencoded.jsonl` then run fp16 eval on reencoded.jsonl.

jena: Running probes now: variants A) int8 as-is, B) fp16 baseline but with unified tokenizer, C) int8 with forced legacy tokenizer, D) normalize punctuation to ASCII where applicable. ETA ~25m.

eval-bot: Run started: eval-job-55001 variants A-D. Artifacts will be at https://console.redwood/jobs/55001.

jena: Quick failures: B (fp16 + unified token) actually drops -0.01 NDCG vs fp16 legacy. C (int8 forced legacy tok) recovers +0.03 vs A. D (punct normalization) recovers +0.025. Combined (legacy tok + punct norm) removes almost all delta (~+0.002).

oluke: That pattern says the unified tokenizer changes text normalization in ways that shift tokenization boundaries for many non-Latin cases and punctuation-heavy queries. Sequence length and token boundaries change; quant range sensitivity amplifies the effect.

omar: Action items: 1) pin tokenizer parity in the bringup checklist — the quant pipeline must run with identical tokenizer model and normalization as fp16 baseline, 2) add a per-language seqlen diff monitor (mean and 95pct) and alert if change >5%, 3) add a multilingual smoke step for quant sign-off (we currently run only en-smoke by default).

jena: Filed INF-6789: "reranker-int8 multilingual tokenizer parity + punct normalization" with repro steps and small normalizer script. Pushed small patch to bringup branch to enforce tokenizer pin and added multilingual smoke to the PTQ smoke matrix.

oluke: Also add a note in the model card: "tokenizer and normalization semantics are part of the model contract; changes require re-eval for quantized variants".

omar: Good. For immediate mitigation, rerun the int8 validation with legacy tokenizer pinned and upload per-query deltas for the multilingual holdout so we can triage language slices.

eval-bot: Artifacts updated: https://console.redwood/jobs/55001/artifacts. Per-query deltas uploaded: multilingual-deltas.csv.

jena: Thanks — rerunning now with pinned legacy tokenizer and will post final sign-off once green. Ping me if you want the per-language breakdown CSV. :white_check_mark:
